messages.subject: workshop
parts:
Hi everyone,

Marc Kéry, Andy Royle and myself are offering a workshop on modeling abundance, distribution, and species richness using unmarked and WinBUGS. The workshop will take place here at Patuxent, April 2-5, 2012. Details can be found here: https://sites.google.com/site/unmarkedinfo/home/workshops.

Richard


_____________________________________
Richard Chandler, post-doc
USGS Patuxent Wildlife Research Center
301-497-5696

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] workshop
parts:
Hi Richard,
 
I would absolutely love to take this workshop but my department might not be willing to pay travel.  Before I ask, do you have any plans to offer this course out West or plans to hold a webinar?
 
I am a wildlife biologist for Banff National Park and have been using R for 13 years for our research and monitoring programs.  I have worked through 2/3 of Royle & Dorazio's Hierarchical Modelling Book and would definately benefit from a workshop.  I've been using your unmarked package, which I really like.  Thank-you for developing it and for posting your course notes.
 
Jesse Whittington
Wildlife Biologst
Banff National Park
Banff, Alberta Canada

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] workshop
parts:
Hi Jesse,

I'm glad you like unmarked. Ian Fiske really deserves most of the credit.

We plan on offering a brief webinar this winter on the use of unmarked, but it will be very basic. We will probably cover some features that make unmarked unique, like the distance sampling models and the open N-mixture models. The workshop will be much more in-depth and will cover both frequentist and Bayesian methods.

Richard

_____________________________________

USGS Patuxent Wildlife Research Center
